newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chinese Estates, Hysan in property deal.
newsitem.headline: Chinese Estates, Hysan in property deal.

text.p: Chinese Estates Holdings Ltd said on Friday it had agreed to sell the entire issued share capital of South Eagle Investments Ltd to Hysan Development Ltd for a total cash consideration of HK$3.64 billion.
South Eagle is the owner of the Entertainment Building in Hong Kong's Central district, it said in a statement.

Chinese Estates said it had received an initial deposit of HK$50 million and a further deposit of HK$310 million would be receivable on December 3. The balance of HK$3.28 billion will be received on completion of the deal on May 20, 1997.
The property generated profits before tax of about HK$69.6 million and HK$105.60 million for the years ended December 31, 1994 and 1995, respectively, Chinese Estates said.
The proceeds of the sale would be used to reduce the group's bank borrowings, for working capital and to fund new potential business opportunities, it added.
The property, a 34-floor commercial and office building, had been held by Chinese Estates as an investment property and was valued at HK$2.95 billion as at December 31, 1995, it said.
